title: Bluehaven - embeddings / rerank discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Bluehaven's search/rerank use case: currently using BM25 + Algolia for product search, evaluating embeddings + reranking with Redwood. Key concerns: throughput for tail-latency <100ms, vector DB integration (Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus), embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), hybrid search (BM25 + vector), data residency and VPC option for PII, SOC2/KMS. Next steps: send pricing for hosted vs dedicated pilot, share security pack and VPC integration notes, run small benchmark with customer's sample dataset.
topics: current stack: Algolia + ES for product search
goal: improve relevance with embeddings + transformer reranker
vector DB choices: Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus
throughput and latency targets: 100ms tail for top-K retrieval + rerank
embedding dimensionality tradeoffs: 768 vs 1536 vs custom
hybrid search: BM25 + vector fusion strategies
deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency
action_items: Maya: send hosted vs dedicated pricing + pilot terms by 2027-04-24
Diego: share benchmark template and sample query set by 2027-04-25
Aisha: provide ~10k sample product catalog + 200 queries by 2027-04-26
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, dataflow, KMS)
Schedule 60m SE deep-dive to run initial benchmark (Diego + Samir)
Start 2-week hosted pilot with 10k vectors, compare 768 vs 1536 embeddings
Discuss Dedicated capacity pricing if throughput exceeds hosted limits
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Bluehaven Head of Search), Tom Riley (CTO), Samir Gupta (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, with Diego on the line, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Aisha: Good, thanks. Excited to talk through embeddings and rerank, we've had some prototypes but need to understand production tradeoffs.
[00:18] Diego: Nice. Can you give a quick overview of your current search stack and where you'd like to improve?
[00:25] Tom: Sure. We run Algolia for product search for our storefront, and an Elastic cluster for site-wide search and analytics. Algolia handles the initial ranking with BM25-ish rules and feature boosts. We want embeddings to improve semantic matches and then a transformer reranker for top 10 results.
[00:40] Samir: Right now relevance suffers on long-tail queries and synonyms. Also facet/filters interplay is messy with vector-only approaches. We're interested in hybrid search — BM25 to surface candidates, then vector similarity and rerank.
[00:55] Maya: Totally makes sense. Typical pattern we see is hybrid: use your inverted index to get 100-200 candidates, then embed + ANN search to rerank or do final scoring. Question on throughput — what are your SLOs?
[01:05] Aisha: For storefront we want p95 end-to-end under 150ms, tail ideally <200ms during spikes. For product detail/faceted search, longer is ok, but checkout is sensitive.
[01:16] Diego: That's reasonable. For a hosted model path we can keep p95 under ~120ms for small payloads, but depends on model size and whether you run a separate transformer reranker. If you run a transformer reranker synchronously for top-10, add ~50-120ms depending on model.
[01:30] Tom: Is that with Redwood hosted or Dedicated?
[01:33] Diego: Hosted, with smaller open models and optimized runtime. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower variance; we can tune for lower tail latencies and higher throughput. Private (VPC) adds network overhead but gives you data residency and control.
[01:46] Aisha: We're also evaluating Pinecone and Weaviate for ANN. How does Redwood fit with vector DBs?
[01:51] Maya: Redwood integrates with vector stores via standard APIs — we can push embeddings out to Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus, or host embeddings in Redwood and perform the ANN locally in the runtime. Many customers use Pinecone for scale but we can demo both.
[02:05] Samir: For dimensionality, we've seen embeddings in 768 and 1536. Any guidance?
[02:10] Diego: Tradeoff: higher dims (1536) tend to capture more nuance but increase storage and ANN cost ~2x and can slightly impact latency. For reranking workflows, 768 often suffices for retrieval combined with a reranker that sees the full text. The pilot approach: test 768 vs 1536 on your workload.
[02:28] Aisha: For hybrid search — do you recommend score fusion or reranking stage?
[02:33] Diego: Both are viable. Common is retrieve via BM25 for recall, run ANN on combined set or rerank top-N with a transformer. Score fusion (normalize BM25 + vector scores) works but reranking with a cross-encoder typically gives the best final relevance at cost of latency.
[02:50] Tom: What about throughput? If we have 200 reqs/s peak, will hosted handle that?
[02:55] Maya: Hosted can handle modest bursts, but sustained 200 req/s with synchronous reranking may push you to Dedicated. Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and throughput scaling — we can size a pool to meet 200 req/s with an X model + batching. We'll need to run benchmarks with your queries.
[03:12] Samir: Any quality/regression tooling? We need to ensure reranker doesn't degrade ranking for two weeks after rollout.
[03:18] Diego: We have Redwood Optimize suggestions and builtin evals — you can push labeled query sets and track P@K, MRR, and automated regression alerts. Also A/B/ canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model.
[03:30] Aisha: Security — SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency — can you support VPC and customer-managed keys?
[03:36] Maya: Yes. Hosted has SOC2 and encryption at rest, we offer a Private deployment option for VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC role controls. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[03:52] Tom: Network-wise, how does VPC connectivity work? Are there egress considerations?
[03:56] Diego: For Private/VPC, control plane sits in your network or we provide a customer VPC peering arrangement; for on-prem you can run a package. There's some network setup but we document it. Small note — KV cache in the runtime (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) is useful for prompt-heavy flows.
[04:12] Aisha: Good. About cost — can you give a rough estimate for embeddings + rerank pilot?
[04:16] Maya: Roughly, hosted embeddings/ANN for 10k vectors and light traffic is inexpensive — we can offer a short pilot credit or discounted pilot. Reranker costs depend on model. We'll send a pricing sheet comparing hosted vs dedicated monthly commitments.
[04:28] Samir: For the pilot, here's what we propose: 10k product vectors, 200 queries, compare retrieval + rerank latency and precision for 768 vs 1536 embeddings.
[04:36] Diego: That's perfect. We'll run an initial bench with Redwood hosted runtime and your sample set, then discuss Dedicated sizing if numbers exceed hosted envelope.
[04:46] Aisha: Any gotchas we should know about integration with Algolia? We want to keep facets and boost rules.
[04:52] Diego: Integrate by keeping Algolia as primary for facets + filters, use it to produce candidate set, then call Redwood/ANN to re-score. We can ship SDK snippets for hybrid pipelines. Watch out for normalization of scores between Algolia and vector distance — we provide guidance.
[05:08] Tom: Competitors — do customers sometimes choose Pinecone + OpenAI embeddings?
[05:12] Maya: Yes, many combos exist. Redwood's value is the inference runtime plus rollout/observability — if you want lower unit costs and an ops story, we bring the serving + routing + caching optimizations.
[05:24] Samir: Any recommendations on embedding model? Open-source vs API?
[05:28] Diego: If data residency or cost is a concern, open-source embeddings (e.g., 768 dense models) are fine. We also support hybrid where embeddings are generated in your infra and Redwood only handles rerank; or we host embeddings. Pilot will help decide.
[05:42] Aisha: Ok that all sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[05:46] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing for hosted vs dedicated pilot, security pack, and a benchmark template. We'll schedule a 60m technical deep dive for the benchmark with Diego + Samir. Bluehaven to share sample dataset and queries.
[06:00] Tom: Sounds good.
[06:02] Aisha: One last question — does Redwood support older vector indexes like HNSW and IVF?
[06:06] Diego: Yes, runtime supports HNSW and can interop with stores using IVF; choice depends on recall/latency tradeoffs. We'll include recommended settings for HNSW ef/construction and quantization tips.
[06:18] Maya: Great — we'll follow up by end of week. Thanks everyone.
[06:22] Aisha: Thanks!
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (KV cash, run-on lines) and speaker overlaps typical of recorded calls.
